pr_title: kubelet: Fix race when KillPod followed by IsPodPendingTermination

/kind bug

<!--

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:

/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

In kubelet, we can't consistently use `IsPodPendingTermination` and `KillPod` since there is a race condition.
When we call `KillPod`, the buffered channel receives the request and `KillPod` is returned. Then `PerformPodKillingWork` fetches the request and adds the given pod to the `terminationMap`. In the meantime, the caller may call `IsPodPendingTerminationByUID` which could return false because `terminationMap` has not yet been set.

This PR
1. ensures the pod to be pending termination or be killed, after `(*podKillerWithChannel).KillPod` has been returned
1. fixes `TestSyncPodsDeletesWhenSourcesAreReadyPerQOS` by simulating `Runtime.KillPod`


Related to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/98893

My goal was to centralize the lock into the podTerminationMap and mirrorPodTerminationMap. Which effectively should be the same thing as the killing Set

@rphillips 

> /lgtm cancel
> 
> I'm getting a deadlock with the TestSyncPodsDeletesWhenSourcesAreReadyPerQOS test

There are two reasons for the timeout,
1. Every `HandlePodCleanUp` calls `podKiller.KillPod` because `FakeRuntime.KillPod` does not clear `FakeRuntime.PodList` which is the list of pods to be killed by next `HandlePodCleanUp`. As a result, it is possible that every `HandlePodCleanUp` cannot call `Destroy` if the pod is pending termination for each call.
2. (Rarely happened?) If 1 were resolved, All of `HandlePodCleanUp` cannot call `Destroy` if the pod is pending termination for more than 2 seconds.

review_comments: checkAndMarkPodPendingTerminationByPod adds the pod to the killing mutex... Adding the mutex and set back to this function is effectively the same functionality as checkAndMarkPodPendingTerminationByPod
Ahh. This synchronizes the killing goroutine on 1289, but the killing pod should be in the map.
We don't have to check it here anymore because I have limited to one request per pod in buffered channel.
